title: Task-first route and responsibility map (G0 freeze)
scopeNote: This contract freezes routes and responsibilities only. Production UI implementation belongs to G9; no production UI is built in G0.

primaryEntryDefinitions.today-review: Today / Review — the task-first main entry: persistent Review queue, actionable Attention, current question and task, recent canonical changes.
primaryEntryDefinitions.project: Project — current research state: Brief, Decisions, Evidence, Issues, Episode relations, contextual Memory, History as secondary content.
primaryEntryDefinitions.search: Search — revision-bound full-text and structured search across canonical objects and history with provenance and authority labels.
primaryEntryDefinitions.settings: Settings — Provider, Privacy & Network, Appearance & Accessibility, Recovery & Data, Integrations, About & Release Proof, Advanced Diagnostics.

routes.label: Today / Review
routes.userAuthoritySurface: Queue items navigate into the Review Thread; no effect is formed here. Recovery notices route to the Recovery gate which locks writes.
routes.note: All projections carry their source projectStateRevision.

routes.label: New Review
allowedDomainObjects: Review draft (suggestion, source provenance, requested target hint)
Host draft queue when the bridge is enabled
routes.userAuthoritySurface: Draft creation only; the draft never mutates canonical state.
routes.note: Manual paste, clipboard import, Host, Skill, and legacy conversions all land here as the same draft schema.

routes.label: Review Thread
allowedDomainObjects: resulting object and Receipt after commit
routes.userAuthoritySurface: The only surface that commits a CanonicalEffect: the user's explicit decision step after the effect preview, enforced by the Kernel.
routes.note: The route is a transport; the Kernel is the only effect executor.

routes.label: Project
routes.userAuthoritySurface: Read-only projections; navigation into Brief edit creates candidates only.
routes.note: Object details are secondary content, not a first-level navigation.

routes.label: Brief detail
routes.userAuthoritySurface: Read-only; coverage is derived and never blocks user authority.
routes.note: Coverage is a derived hint, not a score.

routes.label: Edit Brief
routes.userAuthoritySurface: Creates a persistent Brief candidate only; the candidate becomes canonical exclusively through a patch_brief or formal_direction_change effect committed in a Review.
routes.note: JSON editing is a read-only technical view; typed forms are the editing surface.

routes.label: History
routes.userAuthoritySurface: Read-only audit; export and restore are the only actions.
routes.note: Legacy items always carry an explicit legacy badge and source kind.

routes.label: History detail
routes.userAuthoritySurface: Read-only; a legacy Room or Pilot may be explicitly converted into a new Review draft from here.
routes.note: Conversion copies candidate text and provenance only; it never copies host commands, paths, or secrets.

routes.label: Search
allowedDomainObjects: revision-bound search results across canonical objects and history
routes.userAuthoritySurface: Read-only; results show authority and provenance classes.
routes.note: Index lag is displayed with the projection revision and a rebuild action, never as current truth.

routes.label: Settings
routes.userAuthoritySurface: App-level settings only; Provider test is metadata-only with no research context. Destructive actions (forget, restore, disable bridge) require explicit user confirmation.
routes.note: Provider settings changes never advance projectStateRevision; they only make Manifests stale.

routes.label: Settings section
routes.userAuthoritySurface: Same as Settings; no research effect can be formed here.

recoveryEntry: Recovery is reached from the startup blocking state and from Settings > Recovery. It runs read-only preflight, migration preview, backup verification, and restore previews with all project writes locked; it never fabricates a way to force-open a corrupt or future-schema project.
errorDegradation: Error and degradation states are honest per-surface: stale shows the changed objects and revisions with a rebuild action; Provider failures never disable effects; uncertain attempts are shown as possibly-sent with no automatic retry; projection rebuilds display their source revision; corruption and future schema fail closed into Recovery.
